column2: 0. Personal readiness
Set your monthly budget and the amount you can invest
Build an emergency fund and write a personal investment statement
The emergency fund is built and the personal statement is written
1. Basics
Work out real returns, get to know the market institutions, find the Akhza rate
Find 10 tickers and record the market of each (TSE, Farabourse, base market)
You can explain in 5 minutes why a 40% return may be a loss
2. Codal
Find and summarise each type of report, read the auditor’s paragraphs
Enter the last 12 monthly reports of 3 companies into a spreadsheet; summarise 10 key notes for each
You can split sales growth into volume and price without a guide
3. FIS skills
Normalise profit, build sustainable EPS, payback and sensitivity
A full model of 5 companies; weigh one real capital increase with table 4.5; fill in the Golden Three for 3 dividend-focused stocks with Codal numbers
Your quarterly forecast was off by less than 15% in 3 of 5 companies
Have written rules for buying, selling and position size
Fill in the decision notebook for 8 weeks in a row
In a volatile week you made no trades outside your plan
5. Putting it all together
Build a portfolio from the 5-stage funnel and update it with the 7 steps after every report
A 3-month paper portfolio with monthly updates
For each stock you have the reason for buying, the selling condition and the best opposing argument in 3 lines
6. Advanced
Analyse a holding, a bank and a currency-earning company
Work out an investment company’s NAV from its monthly portfolio report
You can say how much a 20% rise in the dollar changes the EPS of each company in your portfolio
Model an unfamiliar company from scratch in 3 hours: sustainable EPS, payback, 3 red or green flags
Turn a real material-information announcement into its rial effect on EPS in 15 minutes
Judge a capital-increase justification report as value-creating or dilutive, with a numerical reason
A 6-month paper portfolio with a complete notebook, compared with the index and fixed income
Find one of your own wrong decisions and write which bias caused it
Work out the financial freedom formula with your own real monthly costs and the paper portfolio’s dividend yield, and write down the gap
